  "text": "The hardware shop still had her father’s handwriting in the window: KEYS CUT WHILE YOU WAIT.

Nina let herself in through the side door. Behind the counter, her mother was sorting screws into a biscuit tin.

“I thought the man was coming today.”

“Thursday.”

“It is Thursday.”

Her mother checked the calendar beside the till, then pressed its curled corner flat.

“He said after lunch.”

Nina put down her bag. Half the shelves were empty. Pale rectangles showed where packets of hinges had hung for years.

“What shall I do?”

“Those drawers need checking.”

The first contained washers. The second held elastic bands, a pencil stub, and a photograph of a dog neither of them had owned.

“Keep or throw?”

Her mother looked over.

“That was Mr Bell’s. He used to bring it in.”

“The dog?”

“Both.”

Nina set the photograph beside the till.

At twelve, her mother took two sandwiches from her handbag. They ate sitting on the stools her father had forbidden customers to use.

A van stopped outside. Her mother wrapped the remaining half of her sandwich.

But the driver went into the bakery next door.

“There’s no hurry,” Nina said.

“I know.”

Under the counter, Nina found her father’s green flask. She unscrewed the lid. It smelled faintly of coffee.

“Do you want this?”

Her mother held out her hand.

For a moment Nina thought she would put it in her bag. Instead, she carried it to the little sink and filled it with hot water.

“The seal’s good,” she said, turning it upside down.

They watched for a leak. None came."
